title: What is known about 1RB1LE_0LC1RE_---1LD_0RD1LA_0RF1RF_1RA0LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LE_0LC1RE_---1LD_0RD1LA_0RF1RF_1RA0LB.
intro: This six-state, two-symbol Turing machine, one of the holdouts of the BB(6) search, halts when started on a blank tape, after about 1.27·10<sup>758</sup> steps. The exact step is known. It comes from an accelerated simulation that is exact and was checked in several independent ways; its central rule is proved in Lean, the composition of the whole run into one Lean theorem is not done.
verdict: The machine halts (trusted computation). At the visits of the right end the tape is a short front, a ladder of levels (a rung of n blocks 0111111111 and one of eight separator words) and a tail at the left end. Every level is a digit with 16 positions: a hit from the right moves it to the next position, at ten positions the hit is absorbed, at six it is passed on to the left. What lies left of a level therefore lives exactly as it would right behind the front, only 8/3 times slower. After the reset of step 27,167,343, which turned the old ladder into fuel, the tail eats two fuel blocks and leaves three new levels in every 12 hits. With 887 levels the fuel is used up, the next hit runs into the blank left end, and state C reads a 0: the halt, at a step with 759 digits.

claims.title: The machine halts, at a step with 759 digits
Independent re-computation of the halt
claims.text: A second implementation of the level odometer, written separately (its own cell simulator, its own measured step constants, the deepest level always simulated cell by cell), gives the same 887 levels, the same tail, the same last visit and the same 759-digit halting step. Direct simulation agrees with the accelerated run at 12,169 checkpoints in 440 windows spread over the whole run (visit number, step count and whole tape), and about 80 truncated endgames run directly to the halt stop at exactly the predicted step (the longest after 4,568,217,938,175 steps). Not observed directly: anything between step 1.2×10<sup>12</sup> and the halt with more than about 14 levels on the tape; the composition over the 887 levels is not a Lean theorem.

claims.title: The level rules, for every block count
claims.text: A level 4n s is the cells s (0111111111)n. For each of its 16 positions and each stretch of a hit between two crossings of the level's borders, the machine's run is proved for every n ≥ 1 and every tape left and right of the level (63 theorems). A 64th and 65th theorem, last_visit_run and last_visit_halts, run the last visit on the word with all 887 levels removed (2 1 0 3 1 0 3 1 0 5, blank to the left): it halts after 278 steps. The generator checks that the stretches chain as the table says: the states in which the head leaves and comes back, that an absorbing level never touches the tape to its left, and the level after the hit.

claims.title: The level table and all step constants against the machine
claims.text: For 16 positions, 28 block counts (1..24, 40, 77, 200, 1000) and 13 different tapes to the left: the double visit of front + level + rest gives the level of the table and the rest that the front alone would have made of it, the head crosses the borders in the listed states, and the steps inside the level are 112 n + c (H-hit) or 56 n + c (V-hit). 5,656 cases.

claims.title: Visit numbers and step counts equal the direct run's
claims.text: At all 291 compared visits up to step 1.18·10<sup>11</sup> the accelerated run has the visit number and the step count of a direct cell-by-cell run, in three variants (0, 1 or 2 levels kept in the simulated word; started at visit 3,040 or 600). The run started at visit 600 meets the reset of visit 3,006 at the right visit.

claims.title: The same halt with every level simulated at first
claims.text: Keeping the 1, 2 or 3 deepest levels in the simulated word (each level is then run cell by cell for its first hits, and no level ever has to be put back) gives the same 887 levels, the same tail, the same visit number and the same halting step.

claims.title: The last visit, directly
claims.text: Eight tapes with the 887 levels at their final positions, small block counts and the final tail 0 3 1 0 3 1 0 5: the direct run halts in C at the left edge after exactly the number of steps the formula for the last visit gives.

claims.title: One Lean theorem for the halt
claims.text: Not done: the induction over the list of levels (from the level theorems) and the 3,539 simulated hits as a checked certificate would make the halt a Lean theorem.
claims.where: README, How the halting step is found

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: Closed tape languages from windows of 4, 6 and 8 cells cover the run; each allows the halting transition C0 only at the left end (blank to the left) with the right side starting 0001, 000110, 00011001 respectively. Two abstract configurations in all.

claims.title: Whole visits for three families of words
claims.text: Reading pairs from the head leftwards (X = 0 1, Y = 1 1): V(X U) = Y Y U; V(Y3j+1 X U) = X X (Y X X)j Y U; V(Y3j+3 X U) = X X (Y X X)j Y3 U; V(Y3j+2 X X U) ends in X Y4 U. For every j and every tape to the left, 28j + const steps.

claims.title: A tape that halts at the left edge
claims.text: On the tape 0∞ 0 1 1 1 1 1 A> the visit runs into the blank left end and halts after 17 steps. Not a tape of the run from blank.

claims.title: The visit map as a recursion on words
claims.text: V(X U) = Y Y U, V(Y X U) = X X Y U, V(Y Y X X U) = X Y<sup>4</sup> U, V(Y Y Y S) = X X Y V(S), V(Y Y X Y Y S) = X Y<sup>4</sup> V(S): equal to the machine on 19,312 random words and on the 724 visits they cover among the first 1,012 of the run. The words starting Y Y X Y X follow further rules not yet written down.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>12</sup> steps
claims.text: A direct simulator on blocks of 16 cells (a full lookup table, 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps a second) runs 10<sup>12</sup> steps without a halt; the head comes to the left end only at steps 1,779 and 27,158,883.

claims.title: No halt in the first 6.00×10<sup>19</sup> steps (exact macro run)
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 10 cells, long runs of equal blocks crossed in one go; exact: every macro step is a run of the machine, counted step for step) ran from blank tape to step 60,000,783,412,981,265,560 without a halt. At this block size it gives the same state, head position and tape as the direct simulator after 2,000,002,519 steps. This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

check: python3 accel.py                    # the run to the halt (20 s); --defer 1, 2, 3: the same result
python3 accel.py levels             # the level table and step constants against the machine
python3 accel.py last               # the last visit on small tapes, direct run against formula
python3 accel.py check /tmp/v.txt   # visit numbers and step counts against the direct run

explainer.lede: It halts, after about 1.27·10<sup>758</sup> steps. The machine keeps a ladder of counters at the right end of its tape. Each counter is invisible to everything left of it, so the far left of the tape runs the same program in extreme slow motion. There the ladder's tail eats the remains of an earlier ladder; when they are used up, the head steps off the left end of the tape and the machine stops.

facts.text: At a step with 759 digits, about 1.27·10<sup>758</sup> (exact accelerated simulation).
Every level of the ladder is a digit with 16 positions; its rules are proved in Lean for every size.
The ladder at the halt; each level works 8/3 times slower than the one before.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.527).
After 109 steps the tape spans 41,692 cells (5 left of the start, 31,830 right), with a density of 1s of 0.725.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Pairs, digits, and a front
html: Stop the machine each time its head, in state A, stands on the blank cell right of everything it has written (a visit). Read the tape from the head leftwards two cells at a time: X is the pair 0 1, Y is 1 1; nothing else occurs. Write the lengths of the runs of Y between the X's as digits, so 2 1 4 4 is Y Y X Y X Y Y Y Y X Y Y Y Y. Each visit makes the word one pair longer.

At every second visit the word has the same build:

front   4^n1 s1   4^n2 s2   ...   4^nk sk   tail

The front is 2 1 or 5, in turn. A level is a rung of n blocks 4 (on the tape: 0111111111) followed by a separator s, one of eight short words. The tail is what is left over, down to the blank left end. Going from the front 2 1 the head makes what we call an H-hit on the rest of the word, from 5 a V-hit; then a short visit of 8 steps turns the front into the other one.

So the ladder is an odometer: the first level turns with every hit of the front, the second with 6 of every 16 hits of the first, and so on. This table is proved in Lean for every rung length and every surrounding tape (lean/Levels.lean).

sections.heading: Levels are transparent
html: A hit on the part of the tape left of some border is always the same short list of calls: the head crosses the border in a certain state and later comes back in a certain state (for a V-hit: in C, back in E; for an H-hit five calls). A level looks at what is to its left only through these calls. And it passes on H-hits and V-hits in turn, exactly as the front does.

So the tape left of a level behaves exactly as if the front stood directly before it. It only gets its hits more rarely. That makes an exact shortcut possible: keep each level as two numbers (position and rung length), computed with exact integer arithmetic, and run the real machine, cell by cell, only on the front followed by the tail. Step counts stay exact too, because a hit costs 112 n + c or 56 n + c steps inside a level with n blocks. py/accel.py does this; up to step 1011 its visit numbers and step counts are those of the plain simulator.

sections.heading: Resets, fuel, and 887 levels
html: A hit that reaches the blank left end of the tape comes back in an unusual state, and that flattens the ladder: one sweep turns every block 4 into 0 3. It happened at visits 3, 11 and 25 and, with a ladder of six levels, at visit 3,006 (step 27,167,343). After a reset a new ladder grows at the right end, and the flattened blocks are fuel for its tail. In a cycle of 12 hits,

the tail uses up two fuel blocks and leaves three new levels behind. But every new level makes the hits on the tail 8/3 times rarer. The fuel left by the reset of visit 3,006 is about 590 blocks, enough for 887 levels: the tail needs about (8/3)887 ≈ 10378 visits to eat its way to the left end, and a visit by then takes about 10379 steps.

sections.heading: Off the edge
html: The machine can only halt in state C on a 0, and C is only entered when B reads a 0 and steps left. Inside the tape every 0 stands alone, so this needs B at the blank left end.

When the fuel is gone, the tail is 0 3 1 0 3 1 0 5 with blank tape behind it, and an H-hit is due. Its first three calls come back as usual. In the fourth the head runs through the tail in state C, turns the last pairs over, and B arrives on the blank cell left of the tape: one step left, C reads a 0, and the machine halts. The halting step (bbchallenge count) is
The earlier arrivals at the left end (visits 3, 11, 25, 3,006) came in other states and only reset the ladder.

sections.heading: What the result rests on
html:
The halt is found by a program, not proved as one theorem. What supports it:

  • the rule for a level is proved in Lean for every rung length (63 theorems, checked by the kernel), and so is the halt of the last visit once the levels are taken out (last_visit_halts), and tested on the machine in 5,656 cases;
  • the accelerated run agrees with a plain run in visit numbers and step counts at all 291 compared visits, up to step 1.18·1011, and predicts the reset of visit 3,006;
  • three other versions of the run, which simulate each new level cell by cell for its first hits, end with the same 887 levels and the same halting step;
  • the last visit, on tapes with the same 887 levels but short rungs, halts under direct simulation after exactly the predicted number of steps.
What is missing for a full formal proof is the induction over the list of levels and the 3,539 simulated hits written as a certificate that Lean checks.

explainer.title: A ladder that eats its own past, and then falls off the edge

family: ladder of self-similar 16-state levels eating a fuel of old blocks
summary: Halts after about 1.27·10^758 steps (exact step known; trusted accelerated simulation, level rules proved in Lean): the tape is an odometer of levels with 16 positions each, transparent to the part left of them; after the reset of step 27,167,343 its tail eats the old blocks, grows 887 levels and then runs into the blank left end in state B.
